transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well... I'm mostly here because people keep acting like I'm imagining things. But I'm not. 

I know the hospital people and... some folks from the agency... they've been watching our house. They even watch my cleaning routes when I'm working. They're just trying to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband. I don't really want to talk about it much, but... that's why I'm here.
How long have you noticed this feeling that you and your husband are being watched?
Well... it's been a while. Maybe... almost a year now. Like 11 months, I guess. That's when I first noticed them. And... the voices, too. They've both been going on for about that long.

Over this past year, have you also had periods where you felt extremely sad, hopeless, or lacking energy for weeks at a time, or on the other end, unusually elated, full of energy, or needing very little sleep?

Well... I don't know about all that. But... I guess there are times when I don't sleep much. 

Like... maybe two or three hours a night. And then I just... wake up. But I'm not tired. I just get up and... I don't know, scrub the floors or sort through all my papers. I just don't need as much sleep as I used to, I suppose.
During those times when you're only sleeping two or three hours, do you notice your mood feeling unusually upbeat, excited, or more energetic than your normal self?

I suppose... there are stretches where I feel, I don't know, bright. Strong. Like I can handle everything just fine on my own. 

But... it's not always like that. If my husband asks what I'm doing, or if a client questions my work... I tend to snap at them. A lot harder than I mean to, I guess. I just... I don't have patience for it then. That's all.
Even during times when you're not feeling that 'bright' or high energy, do you still hear the voices or believe you're being watched?

Yes... even then. 

There was a time... a few weeks, maybe. Things were quieter. I was actually sleeping, not... rushing around so much. But... they were still there. 

I still heard the voice... usually by the kitchen window. And... I still knew the agency was watching us. It didn't stop.
Over this past year, would you say the times without the 'bright, high-energy' feelings—when it's just the voices and the watching—have lasted longer overall than the times when you do feel that way?

No... I don't think so. 

Mostly, since this whole change started... I've just been keyed up. Irritable. Even during the stretches when things aren't at their absolute worst, I just... I feel driven to keep moving. 

So... that part has been most of the time, I guess.
When you're in one of those 'bright, high-energy' stretches, about how many days in a row does that usually last before it eases up?

I'm not sure exactly how many days in a row... I don't really track it like that. 

But... those stretches where I'm all wired up, barely sleeping, and snapping at everyone... they've been coming and going for a while now. Maybe... ten months or so? It just keeps happening.

Has there ever been a stretch of a month or longer where you still heard the voices or felt watched, but your mood and energy were completely normal—not wired, not irritable, just your usual baseline self?

I... I think I mentioned that already. There was that... quieter spell. For a few weeks. 

I was sleeping more. Not rushing around. But... the voice was still there. By the window. And I still knew they were watching. So... yes. A few weeks.
During these times when you're feeling wired and not sleeping much, are you using any caffeine, energy drinks, diet pills, or other stimulant medications or drugs?
No. I don't take anything like that. Just... regular coffee in the morning, sometimes. That's all.

During that quieter few-week period when you were sleeping more and not rushing around, did you also notice any sadness, low mood, or hopelessness, or would you say your mood felt essentially normal for you?
I... I don't know. I don't think so. I was just... quiet. Not sad, really. Just... normal, I guess.
